review_title: Blockchain-Based Land Registry and Land Administration Systems

eligibility_criteria.label: Land registry / land administration relevance
eligibility_criteria.include_guidance: The study addresses blockchain or distributed ledger technology in land registration, cadastral systems, land administration, property rights records, land information systems, or directly relevant property-transfer processes.
eligibility_criteria.exclude_guidance: The study is unrelated to land/property records or land administration.

eligibility_criteria.label: Eligible publication type
eligibility_criteria.include_guidance: The publication type is allowed by the review protocol.
eligibility_criteria.exclude_guidance: The publication type is explicitly disallowed by the protocol (for example, editorial or duplicate record, if the protocol excludes these).

eligibility_criteria.label: Contribution to at least one research question
eligibility_criteria.include_guidance: The study contributes evidence to at least one of RQ1-RQ4: barriers; architecture/security; governance/interoperability; or performance/viability.
eligibility_criteria.exclude_guidance: After full-text assessment, no relevant evidence contributes to any review question.

research_questions.RQ1: Technical, regulatory, interoperability, adoption and deployment constraints affecting blockchain adoption in land registries.
research_questions.RQ2: Hybrid architecture and integration, including Ethereum/EVM, on-chain/off-chain storage, IPFS/databases, validation, security and efficiency.
research_questions.RQ3: Governance, legal validity, compliance, LADM/ISO 19152, standards and integration with legacy cadastral systems.
research_questions.RQ4: Scalability, throughput, latency, consensus overhead, transaction costs and performance under realistic registry workloads.

quality_appraisal.label: Research objective or question is clear
System, legal, institutional or study context is described
Methods or design are sufficiently described
Claims are supported by traceable evidence
Evaluation or argument is appropriate to the study type
Limitations or threats to validity are discussed
Data, implementation details, metrics or procedures are sufficiently reproducible
